summary: This is a re-audit of a corrective fix (commit f4f70f1d) addressing a real PR #596 audit FAIL: generateInterimBill() previously built invoice line items with no taxTemplateId (silently posting $0 GST on every interim/RA bill) and modeled retention as a negative invoice line that would have further shrunk the taxable subtotal once tax was wired in. The fix makes taxTemplateId a required, org-validated input (404 if the template doesn't belong to the org, 400 if omitted), extracts a new pure buildInterimBillInvoiceItems() helper that emits every billable line at its full currentBillAmount carrying the real taxTemplateId with no synthetic retention line, and correctly splits erp-invoicing-service.ts's computeInvoiceTotals() into a pure computeInvoiceTaxTotals() plus a thin DB-fetching wrapper, matching this repo's established pure-function-core testing convention. I independently verified: the sole caller (POST /api/construction/interim-bills) passes the request body straight through so the new required field surfaces correctly as a 400 rather than silently defaulting; the tax math is domain-correct (GST due on full certified value, retention is a separate payment-holdback tracked only in constructionInterimBills.retentionAmount/netPayable, never as a taxable-value-reducing invoice line); the new/updated unit tests directly assert the old-bug shape is gone (no negative line, nonzero tax, full un-reduced gross); the accompanying migration (drizzle/0267, renumbered from 0265 to resolve a collision with 3 other parallel tasks' 0264-0266) is additive-only and RLS policies match the established construction_* table pattern; and no .github/workflows/** files are touched. I ran the actual test and type-check gates myself rather than trusting the self-report: `bun test` on the 4 touched service test files (30/30 pass, 76 expect() calls) and a full-repo `bunx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors). This is a schema/migration-touching change so tier2 classification is correct regardless of my approval; migration application to the live Supabase project and get_advisors(security) remain explicitly deferred to the Owner per the task's own Remaining section, which is the right call for a not-cleanly-reversible action.
